precepts.text: By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you; the Most High cut the army down to able men of His choosing.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
Moses and Aaron numbered every man able to go forth to war by their armies, but the Most High chose able men, and He was never bound to the numbers. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred.

“And the Lord said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place.” He sent the rest home and saved Israel by the three hundred of His choosing.

So the numbering of the armies in Numbers 1 is the numbering of the men the Lord could use, and the Lord chose which able men would win His battles.

precepts.text: Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God in not keeping his commandments; the warning was given before they ever entered the land.
precepts.point: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
The Lord says the people are too many “lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me.” That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think, and he warned about it before they ever entered the land: “Beware that thou forget not the Lord thy God, in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day.”

Forgetting the Lord begins with not keeping his commandments, and it ends with a man saying his own hand saved him. Thinning the army was the Lord keeping Israel from that very thing.

precepts.text: Lest thine heart be lifted up and thou say in thine heart, my power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth; thou shalt remember the Lord thy God, for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.
precepts.point: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Here is the heart the Lord was guarding against when he sent twenty and two thousand home: “Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint; Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not, that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end.”

The danger: “And thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth.” That is the same as “Mine own hand hath saved me.” The correction: “But thou shalt remember the Lord thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.”

That is why God always lowered the numbers going into battle, so Israel would know it was by the Lord's strength that we overcame our enemies. And it is going to be the same thing again: few numbers going into battle against the nations when that time comes.

precepts.text: The same word came to Abraham: get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred; there were things the Lord had to do for him that required letting go.
precepts.point: What can we learn from this? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, of whom I say, this shall not go with thee, the same shall not go: some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
What can we learn from the trying at the water? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, “of whomsoever I say unto thee, This shall not go with thee, the same shall not go.”

The same word came to Abraham: “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee.” There were things the Lord had to do for him that required letting go of his kindred and his father's house. Some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

precepts.text: Christ came to divide and separate, father, mother, husband, wife, family; let that ring in your mind, you have to be willing to let go of some people for the battle ahead.
precepts.point: What can we learn from this? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, of whom I say, this shall not go with thee, the same shall not go: some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Christ came to divide and separate: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

Father, mother, husband, wife, family: let that ring in your mind. Gideon went to the water with ten thousand and came away with three hundred, because the Lord said who would go and who would not. You have to be willing to let go of some people for the battle ahead.

precepts.text: If ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and saved from your enemies. This is the history behind the shofars we blow; those trumpets are not just for looks and thumbnails, there is a deep meaning behind them going into the memorial of blowing of trumpets.
precepts.point: Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies, a hundred to the left flank, a hundred down the middle, a hundred to the right, and puts a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers and lamps within the pitchers. Look on me, and do likewise: pay attention, and when I blow the trumpet, blow ye also on every side of the camp, and say, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Gideon “put a trumpet in every man’s hand” and told them, “When I blow with a trumpet, I and all that are with me, then blow ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp.” That is the law of the trumpets in war: “And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.”

Midian was the enemy that oppressed Israel in their own land, and the three hundred blew the alarm on every side of the camp, to be remembered before the Lord and saved. This is the history behind the shofars we blow. Those trumpets are not just for looks and thumbnails; there is a deep meaning behind them, going into the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

precepts.text: Jerubbaal, who is Gideon; the two names are the same man.
precepts.point: Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh: he reminded them that he was family. When people do that, they want you to remember that blood is thicker than water, so you will back them whether or not it is right.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why: “Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon”: the two names are the same man. So Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal is the son of Gideon, the judge who delivered Israel from Midian, and “the sons of Jerubbaal, which are threescore and ten persons” are Gideon's seventy sons.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return: twenty and two thousand bounced back to Gilead, and ten thousand remained. That is why God always lowered the numbers going into battle, so Israel would know it was by the Lord's strength that we overcame our enemies; and it is going to be the same thing again, few numbers going into battle against the nations when that time comes.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: What can we learn from this? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, of whom I say, this shall not go with thee, the same shall not go: some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The people are yet too many; the Lord tries them at the water. Some lapped the water with their hand to their mouth as a dog lappeth, and all the rest bowed down upon their knees to drink; the lappers were three hundred men.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand. The Lord sent the rest of Israel every man unto his tent and retained the three hundred, with victuals and trumpets in their hands.

Now you know where the famous story of the three hundred came from: they got it from our ancestors, from Gideon. The nations take our history and make it entertainment, and even the artwork drew those three hundred with locks and braids and gave the other host the same, because the artist knew whose history he was drawing; those three hundred were Israelites.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The same night the Lord sends Gideon down to the outside of the enemy host with Phurah his servant: thou shalt hear what they say, and afterward shall thine hands be strengthened. There he hears a man telling his fellow a dream of a cake of barley bread tumbling into the host and overturning a tent, and his fellow interprets it: this is nothing else save the sword of Gideon, for into his hand hath God delivered Midian.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The Lord put that dream into the mind of the enemy and sent Gideon down to hear it, so he could go into the battle valiant and strong, without any doubt. When Gideon heard the dream and the interpretation, he worshipped, and returned to say, arise; for the Lord hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies, a hundred to the left flank, a hundred down the middle, a hundred to the right, and puts a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers and lamps within the pitchers. Look on me, and do likewise: pay attention, and when I blow the trumpet, blow ye also on every side of the camp, and say, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: Gideon and his hundred come to the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch; in war you always have watchmen taking first, second, and third watch, and Gideon struck right in between the changing of the watchmen.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The three companies blew the trumpets, brake the pitchers, held the lamps in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, and cried, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon; and every man stood in his place round about the camp. Three hundred against thousands, you have to do something to mess with their mind: those horns blowing in unison put fear in the nations, and all the host ran, and cried, and fled.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: And the Lord set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host. The enemy destroyed itself; that is the Lord fighting the battle.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The men of Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh gathered themselves and pursued after the Midianites, and Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim to come down and take the waters before them; and Ephraim took two princes of Midian, slaying Oreb upon the rock Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb.

Ephraim, stand up; get this spirit back and come join your brothers in the war, because Judah is calling you right now. For those that may not know, that is you so-called Hispanics, you Puerto Ricans: you are Ephraim.
